title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
experiments_summary: The study evaluates an ensemble consensus semi-supervised learning (SSL) method across multiple settings. A semi-supervised protocol is applied where 10% of training data is labeled and 90% is treated as unlabeled for the consistency loss. The primary baseline is a standard supervised deep ensemble trained only on the labeled subset. Specific experimental setups include: (1) QM9 quantum chemistry benchmark: a four-member PaiNN ensemble predicts 12 molecular properties; ensemble size is varied to study scaling behavior; hyperparameters (learning rate, weight decay) are tuned per target via validation performance on labeled data; coupling weight gamma is swept over {1.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001} and mean-teacher decay over {0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.995, 0.999}. (2) GNN+ benchmark: GCN, GIN, and GatedGCN architectures are tested on a suite of graph-level datasets (ZINC, ogbg-molhiv, ogbg-molpcba, peptides-func, peptides-struct, ogbg-ppa, PascalVOC-SP, CLUSTER, MalNet-Tiny, MNIST, PATTERN) with M=4 ensembles; SSL coupling parameters are selected based on ZINC validation performance. (3) CIFAR-10 vision benchmark: ResNet-18 with 5,000 labeled and 40,000 unlabeled samples is used to study ensemble size scaling beyond 4 members (without data augmentation); an exhaustive hyperparameter sweep is performed over learning rate and weight decay. Comparisons are made against: supervised-only ensembles, mean-teacher, and PSEUDOsigma (re-implemented for PaiNN with an evidential head, 1000-epoch initial training plus 15 episodic episodes of 100 epochs each). Additional ablations investigate: sensitivity of coupling weight gamma on CIFAR-10, linear coupling schedules (constant, increase, bell) and coupling start timing on QM9 targets, hard-labeling vs. soft-labeling consistency targets on ogbg-molhiv, alternative loss functions for the consistency term (L1, L2, L-inf, KL-divergence, reversed KL), calibration metrics (NLL, ECE, MCE) on ogbg-molhiv, and overfitting to unlabeled data by comparing MAE on unlabeled training set vs. test set for all 12 QM9 targets. All results are reported as mean plus/minus 1.96 standard errors across multiple random seeds, with train/validation/test splits of 80/10/10.
